Form Answers: Why are you interested in this role?

At Snabbit, I scaled retention from 20% to 50% and doubled AOV to Rs 2,000 by launching the Blush Prive retention pass. Razorpay is the backbone of that infrastructure.

I want to move from the merchant side to the platform side. These projects proved I can bridge the gap between complex financial logic and scalable product execution. I want to apply that same rigor to Razorpay’s APM role, where product decisions directly impact the efficiency of India’s digital economy.

My background in Economics at IIT Kharagpur, combined with a Micro-Specialization in AI & Applications, allows me to approach payment products with both quantitative precision and technical fluency. I don’t just want to manage features; I want to optimize the financial and operational levers that define Razorpay’s value proposition.

This role sits at the intersection of my strongest assets: data-driven product strategy and financial acumen. I am ready to leverage my experience in scaling high-volume operations—managing 100+ SKUs and Rs 30L working capital at Snabbit—to drive measurable impact on Razorpay’s payment ecosystem.
Why are you interested in this role?

During my internship at Snabbit, I scaled retention GOV from 20% to 50% by launching the Blush Prive retention pass. That experience taught me how to blend data analytics with user experience to drive growth. The role of Product Manager here offers the chance to lead similar initiatives at scale, leveraging my background in building AI‑driven tools at Aequitas and predictive models at Frost & Sullivan. I am drawn to Snabbit’s focus on experiential beauty services, where I can apply my expertise in optimizing SKU portfolios and vendor negotiations, as I did with 100+ SKUs and Rs 30L working capital. The opportunity to shape product strategy for a rapidly growing marketplace aligns with my track record of delivering measurable impact—doubling AOV, cutting vendor costs by 50%, and maintaining 99% fulfillment. I want to bring that data‑centric, execution‑driven mindset to Snabbit’s product team.
Tell me about a time you solved a difficult problem with data.

Reduced forecast error by 30% for a $23 M sales portfolio at Frost & Sullivan by building a predictive time‑series pipeline in Power BI. The team struggled to allocate inventory because monthly sales reports showed high variance and no reliable forward view. I extracted three years of transaction data with SQL, cleaned inconsistencies, and engineered lag features. Using moving‑average and exponential‑smoothing models, I compared out‑of‑sample performance in DAX and selected the model that minimized mean absolute percentage error. I then visualized rolling forecasts, confidence bands, and scenario analyses in a Power BI dashboard shared with senior operations leaders. The new forecast enabled a 15% reduction in safety stock and freed ₹2 L of working capital each month. The solution was adopted across three additional business units, saving the company over ₹6 L annually and establishing a data‑driven planning process that continues to inform quarterly budgeting.
